title: CNP Membership Compilations Have Different Scopes
description_short: Supplied material describes two incomplete CNP membership compilations; it does not establish Donald Trump’s membership or role.
description_medium: Supplied material describes one Council for National Policy compilation as listing 1,011 names from 1981–2020 while covering fewer than half of its members, and a separate 2020 directory said to contain 426 names. The different lists are not a combined membership count. The material does not establish Donald Trump’s membership or any Trump action, so this remains an unverified CNP-history draft.
description_long: This internal draft concerns Council for National Policy (CNP) membership compilations, not a demonstrated Trump action. The supplied material describes a TrumpFile compilation said to cover 1981–2020 and list 1,011 names, while its compiler is described as cautioning that it may contain fewer than half of CNP members. The material also describes a separate leaked September 2020 directory said to name 426 people. Those figures refer to different lists with different dates and scopes; they must not be added or presented as a total membership count. The frozen entry’s January 20, 1981 date does not establish when either directory was created or published. The supplied record does not confirm that Donald Trump appears on any list, joined CNP, attended a CNP event, or took a policy action through the group. Names associated with CNP do not prove Trump’s membership or involvement. Any public version needs direct access to the list pages and a reliable, dated source for a specific Trump connection. Until then, this remains an unverified draft about the claimed scope of CNP lists and is not eligible for publication as a Trump-related event.

title: Vought Ordered CFPB Staff to Stop Work; Court Blocked Further Layoffs
description_short: Vought ordered CFPB staff to stop work on Feb. 10, 2025; a judge blocked more layoffs after over 100 workers had been fired.
description_medium: On February 10, 2025, Acting CFPB Director Russell Vought ordered bureau employees to stop work. A federal judge later blocked additional layoffs after more than 100 workers had been fired that week. The sources support a work stoppage and workforce reduction effort, but do not substantiate the frozen entry’s claim that all roughly 1,700 employees were fired on February 7.
description_long: On February 10, 2025, CFPB Acting Director Russell Vought ordered bureau employees to stop work, according to the District Court’s later account in NTEU v. Vought. The court said the administration was pursuing measures to dismantle the agency, including firings, funding cuts, contract terminations, office closures and a reduction in force. On February 14, NPR reported that a federal judge blocked additional layoffs after more than 100 workers had already been fired that week. The record therefore describes a serious work stoppage and attempted workforce reduction, not a completed firing of the bureau’s full roughly 1,700-person staff. The original February 7 date is not the date of the stop-work order identified in the opinion, and the sources reviewed do not establish that all pending CFPB cases were halted. The injunction was preliminary while litigation continued; it does not by itself decide every underlying legal question. This correction preserves the CFPB action and its immediate legal response while separating completed events from planned reductions. The supplied claim that the bureau’s closure benefited Trump campaign donors is not supported by the sources cited here and is omitted.

title: Trump and Abe Golfed at Trump National in Florida During Abe’s 2017 Visit
description_short: The Feb. 11, 2017 public schedule lists Trump golfing with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe at Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter.
description_medium: On February 11, 2017, President Donald Trump’s public schedule listed him playing golf with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe at Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida. The supplied allegation that Trump showed Abe plans for a Trump-branded course in Japan is not confirmed by that schedule and remains unverified. This correction records the same visit’s documented golf outing without asserting a business pitch.
description_long: On February 11, 2017, President Donald Trump’s public schedule listed a round of golf with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe at Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida. The schedule is the evidence for the date, participants and venue of the outing. It places the golf game within Abe’s official U.S. visit; it does not record their conversation. The frozen description alleged that Trump showed Abe plans for a Trump-branded golf course in Japan and discussed his private golf business. The accessed schedule entry records the golf outing but does not describe what the two leaders said or showed each other. Because a missing mention does not disprove a private conversation, that part remains an allegation requiring a source that reports what was shown or discussed. This corrected draft retains the same February 2017 Abe visit and the golf outing documented by the public schedule. It narrows the event to what the source states and removes claims about a Japanese course proposal, business promotion, or ethics experts’ assessment. It does not imply the outing alone established wrongdoing or that the trip produced a business agreement. Keep the original allegation unpublished unless it can be tied to a contemporaneous credible report or documentary record.
